title: कृषि क्षेत्रमा बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाहरूको लगानी खुम्चिँदै, सातै प्रदेशमा किन घट्यो कर्जा ?
content:
Kathmandu. Investment by banks and financial institutions in the agricultural sector, which is considered the backbone of the country's economy, is shrinking. Various reports by Nepal Rastra Bank have shown that the situation of agricultural credit flow in all seven provinces of Nepal has become worrisome in recent times. The report points out that financial institutions are increasingly de-prioritizing the agricultural sector over total lending. In some provinces, agricultural lending has declined by billions of rupees compared to last year, leaving real farmers without access to credit. Disappointing investment in Bagmati Province The credit flow from banks and financial institutions to the agricultural sector in Bagmati Province has been disappointing. According to a report by Nepal Rastra Bank, in mid-Ashar 2083, credit flow to the agricultural sector in this province has decreased by 0.91 percent compared to the same period of the previous year to 120 billion rupees. While such credit had increased by 1.30 percent last year. Banks and financial institutions in Bagmati Province have disbursed only 3.3 percent of the total credit to the agricultural sector. However, when considering the total agricultural credit across the country, Bagmati Province alone has a share of 36.57 percent. This shows that the total size of this province is larger than that of other provinces. District-wise data within Bagmati Province shows that investment is highly uneven and concentrated in a few specific urban districts. Kathmandu district has the highest share of 52.53 percent of total credit flowing to the agricultural sector. Similarly, Chitwan district has 21.71 percent, Makawanpur 4.76 percent, Kavrepalanchok 4.14 percent and Lalitpur 4.09 percent. In other hilly and mountainous districts of Bagmati, there has been only a nominal flow of credit. Dolakha district has the lowest share of agricultural credit, at just 0.38 percent. Similarly, Rasuwa has 0.55 percent, Sindhupalchowk 0.95 percent, Ramechhap 0.56 percent, Sindhuli 1.58 percent, Nuwakot 2.98 percent, Dhading 3.37 percent and Bhaktapur 2.41 percent. Bankers say that since most of the banks and financial institutions have their headquarters in Kathmandu and their loan limits are approved from those offices, the agricultural loan figures for urban and accessible districts like Kathmandu and Chitwan are high. However, actual agricultural farms or farmers in rural areas still have to struggle to get large amounts of loans easily. Madhesh investment decreased by about 5 percent The agricultural credit situation in Madhesh Province, which is considered a storehouse of grain, is also becoming miserable. In the fiscal year 2082/83, agricultural credit from banks and financial institutions in Madhesh Province decreased by 4.95 percent to 59.56 billion 90 million rupees compared to the same period last year. Such credit was 62.18 billion 40 million rupees in the same period last year. The share of total credit flowing in this province to the agricultural sector is only 12.10 percent. When looking at the distribution of total agricultural credit flowing in the districts of Madhesh Province, a large gap is seen between Sarlahi and Saptari. The share of credit flowing in Sarlahi district is the highest at 16 percent, while Saptari's share is the lowest at 7.69 percent. After that, agricultural credit flow has increased to 15.18 percent in Dhanusha, 14.40 percent in Parsa, 13.81 percent in Siraha, 12.04 percent in Mahottari, 10.90 percent in Bara, and 9.98 percent in Rautahat. Despite the geographical accessibility, abundance of cultivable land, close trade access to the border, and relative ease of transportation in Madhesh Province, the agricultural sector is currently facing various policy and structural challenges due to national and international circumstances. The shrinking investment by banks in Madhesh Province, which has fertile land and high agricultural potential, has severely affected small and commercial farmers in the region. Farmers here, who are suffering from problems of fertilizer, seeds and irrigation, are finding it difficult to get out of the traditional farming system due to the lack of easy credit from financial institutions. The Rastra Bank report has pointed out that the market system is dominated by middlemen due to limited access to market, storage and processing facilities for agricultural produce produced by farmers in this province. Lumbini attracts huge attention in Rupandehi and Dang, but disappointment in others In Lumbini Province, there has also been a contraction in agricultural credit compared to last year. In mid-Ashar 2083, credit flowed to the agricultural sector from banks and financial institutions in this province decreased by 0.90 percent compared to the same period of the previous year, to Rs 50.21 billion. Last year, such credit had decreased by 3.46 percent. Banks and financial institutions in this province have disbursed 8.40 percent of the total loans to the agricultural sector, while the national share of the total agricultural loans disbursed to Lumbini Province is 15.21 percent. The distribution of agricultural credit is unbalanced in different districts of Lumbini. The highest share of credit flowing to the agricultural sector is in Rupandehi district (41.90 percent). Similarly, 15.36 percent has been flowing in Dang district, 12.00 percent in Banke, 10.61 percent in Kapilvastu and 5.30 percent in Nawalparasi (West). In the hilly and remote districts of this province, the agricultural credit situation is very low. Bardiya has 5.50 percent, Palpa 2.22 percent, Gulmi 1.19 percent, Pyuthan 1.14 percent, Rolpa 0.70 percent, Arghakhanchi 0.69 percent and the lowest is Rukum (East) district with only 0.41 percent agricultural credit flow. In Gandaki Province, credit flowing to the agricultural sector is also continuously declining. In this province, agricultural credit flowing to the agricultural sector from banks and financial institutions has decreased by 4.48 percent to Rs 22.29 billion. Last year, such credit had also decreased by 15.26 percent. The share of agricultural credit in the total credit flowing to this province is only 6.32 percent. Looking at the total agricultural loans of Gandaki Province by subheading, it is seen that there is an investment of Rs 22.3 billion in the agriculture and forestry subheading and only Rs 290 million in the fisheries subheading. The graph of Koshy also descends. The graph of agricultural credit flow in Koshi Province has also been declining. In mid-Ashar 2083, credit flow to the agricultural sector of Koshi Province from banks and financial institutions has decreased by 1.1 percent compared to the previous year to 55.686 billion rupees. In mid-Ashar 2082, such credit had also decreased by 6 percent to 56.3 billion rupees. Of the total credit flow in Koshi Province as of mid-Ashar 2083, approximately 639.322 billion rupees were disbursed, of which only 8.7 percent was in the agricultural sector. Looking at the district-wise credit flow from banks and financial institutions to the agricultural sector in Koshi Province, Morang district has the highest amount of Rs 20.9 billion 35 million (37.5 percent) and Taplejung has the lowest amount of Rs 367.2 million (0.7 percent). Although there is a significant amount of agricultural credit flow in Jhapa and Sunsari districts, credit flow has reached a low point in the hilly and mountainous districts of Bhojpur, Solukhumbu, and Taplejung. Looking at the sub-heading status of agricultural credit flow in Koshi Province in the fiscal year 2082/83, it is seen that there was an increase of 71.1 percent in irrigation, 22 percent in other cash crops and 13.7 percent in cotton. However, there was a decrease of 83.3 percent in tobacco, 36.6 percent in seed production and 17 percent in grain storage. Credit drought in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces There has also been a disappointing contraction in credit flow to the agricultural sector in the Far West Province. As of mid-July 2083, credit flow to the agricultural sector in the Far West Province from banks and financial institutions has decreased by 2.13 percent compared to mid-July 2082, reaching 15.62 billion 4.4 million. In the same period last year, such credit had also decreased by 3.41 percent. Out of the total credit flow to this province, the share of credit flowed to the agricultural sector is only 9.56 percent. Out of the nine districts of Sudurpaschim, the distribution of agricultural credit is concentrated in only two districts. Kailali district has the highest share of 67.75 percent of the total credit flowing to the agricultural sector, while Kanchanpur district has the highest share of 20.23 percent. Apart from these two districts, the credit situation in other districts is pathetic. The agricultural credit flow is 3.09 percent in Dadeldhura, 1.93 percent in Darchula, 1.69 percent in Baitadi, 1.63 percent in Bajhang, 1.35 percent in Doti, 1.35 percent in Achham and the lowest in Bajura district at only 0.98 percent. This data shows that commercial agricultural credit has not reached the hilly and mountainous districts except Kailali and Kanchanpur in the Far West. Similarly, despite being geographically remote and having great potential for agriculture, investment by banks and financial institutions in Karnali Province has been declining. Compared to mid-July 2082, credit disbursed to the agricultural sector by banks and financial institutions in this province has decreased by 1.56 percent to Rs 4.9 billion 6.9 billion in mid-July 2083. Of the total agricultural loans disbursed in Karnali Province, the highest amount of Rs 1.114 billion has been disbursed under the livestock farming and slaughterhouse category. District-wise, out of the 10 districts of Karnali, the highest amount of Rs 1.6 billion has been disbursed in Surkhet district, while the lowest amount of Rs 1.34 billion has been disbursed in Mugu district. Looking at the share of different districts in Karnali Province, Surkhet has the highest loan flow of 32.79 percent. This is followed by Rukum West with 13.02 percent, Salyan with 12.22 percent, Jajarkot with 8.26 percent, Dailekh with 7.61 percent, Jumla with 11.11 percent, Humla with 5.58 percent, Dolpa with 3.60 percent, Kalikot with 3.32 percent and Mugu with 2.74 percent.
